properties.areaDesc: Southern Susitna Valley; Central Susitna Valley
properties.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued October 20 at 2:52AM AKDT until October 20 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog.

* WHERE...Central Susitna Valley and Southern Susitna Valley.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to low visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An area of locally dense fog has developed
along the Parks Highway from north of Willow to the Talkeetna Spur
Road. Patchy dense fog is expected to persist across portions of
the Susitna Valley through mid morning Tuesday. The fog may lift
periodically during times of falling snow and rain.
properties.instruction:
A dense fog advisory means visibilities will frequently be reduced to
less than one quarter mile. If driving, slow down, use your
headlights, and leave plenty of distance ahead of you.

properties.areaDesc: Thompson Pass
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 20 at 2:48AM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Additional snow accumulations between 10 and
16 inches, mainly near the top of the pass.

* WHERE...Thompson Pass.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery
roads.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A long duration snowfall event will continue
through tonight. Temperatures at of slightly above freezing will
allow snow to change to rain at times for lower elevations of the
pass. At the top of the pass, snow will be more prolonged but may
also briefly mix with rain at times.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.areaDesc: Anchorage; Lower Matanuska Valley; Sutton / Upper Matanuska Valley
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 20 at 2:48AM AKDT until October 20 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 2 and 6
inches, highest amounts near the mountains.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of Anchorage and the Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM AKDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery
roads. Visibilities as low as one half mile possible, including
during the morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Rain will intensify during the overnight hours
and change to snow late tonight through early Tuesday morning, with
temperatures falling to near freezing. The heaviest snow and
highest accumulation will be near the mountains, from the lower
Anchorage Hillside to East Anchorage and up the Glenn Highway
corridor to Palmer and Sutton. Roads will start out wet and road
surface temperatures are still warm (in the upper 30s), but steady
moderate snow should be enough to lead to slushy accumulation,
especially along neighborhood roads. Snow will change back to rain
by late morning in south to west Anchorage, continue northward to
the Matanuska Valley in the afternoon. The exact timing of
changeover back to rain will greatly impact total snow amounts.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

NWSheadline: WINTER WEATHER ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 1 PM AKDT THIS AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Cape Fairweather to Lisianski Strait
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 20 at 2:44AM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
An atmospheric river, currently over the Yakutat area, is expected
to continue through today. Multiple periods of heavy rain are
expected for the Icy Strait corridor and northeast Gulf Coast,
including the following communities: Yakutat, Elfin Cove, Pelican,
Gustavus, Juneau. Elevated gusty winds are expected alongside this
heavier rainfall, with the strongest winds from the southwest
expected late this morning into this afternoon. Prolonged periods of
moderate to heavy rain will produce significant river rises with the
potential for at least minor flooding in Juneau and Gustavus. Ponding
of water in low-lying areas is also possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Eastern Gulf Coast and Northeast Gulf
Coast. This includes the cities of Elfin Cove And Pelican.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals for the Elfin Cove and Pelican area through this
evening range between 3-4 inches, with greater than 6 inches
possible at elevations greater than 1000 ft. Coinciding with high
rain rates, possibly exceeding 0.3 inches per hour, elevated wind
gusts greater than 40 mph are expected at elevations greater than
500 ft.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

humidity will fall below 25 percent for much of the afternoon,
especially for northeast Georgia. Given the dry vegetation,
outdoor fires will be able to spread quickly once started,
increasing the danger of wildfires.

fires can quickly get out of hand under these conditions.
